items.title: Washington’s diplomacy in Sudan has backfired
items.description: Pressure meant to isolate Sudan’s army has instead left Washington isolated and a ceasefire further out of reach.

items.title: Ethiopia and Eritrea cut diplomatic ties as northern conflict escalates
items.description: The diplomatic fallout comes as Ethiopian forces battle rebel fighters across its northern region.

items.title: Ukraine, South Korea clash over transfer of 2 North Korean prisoners
items.description: A diplomatic scandal has erupted over two North Korean prisoners of war, with South Korea demanding an apology from Ukraine. What's been the reaction in Kyiv?

items.title: War in Ukraine: 'First surrender, then negotiation. These are Moscow's words'
items.description: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov's claim at the UN that Europe, unlike the US, is undermining peace talks on Ukraine is a double falsehood, writes Le Monde columnist Alain Frachon.

items.title: Houthi militia now leads Iran’s ‘Axis.’ But how much can Tehran count on it?
items.description: Iranian officials and pundits laud the militia group’s gains as their own. At the same time, some media coverage appears designed to convince the Houthis to be better team players.

items.title: Sledgehammer for Putin
items.description: Congress has handed President Trump a sweeping sanctions bill, signed Sept. 18, that lets him hit Russia's oil, banks, and buyers like China and India by Oct. 18 unless Moscow agrees to peace talks. items.title: Russian Orthodox Church Denies That Troops Lost Medieval Warrior Prince’s Relics in Ukraine
items.description: Pro-war Telegram channels reported that Russian forces may have lost the relics during a withdrawal in Ukraine’s Donetsk region.

items.title: What life under U.S. sanctions looks like for one ICC judge
items.description: Kimberly Prost, a Canadian judge at the International Criminal Court, says U.S. sanctions disrupted her daily life. She is still hearing cases and challenging the sanctions in court.

items.title: Malaysia: UN agency urges safeguards after refugees returned to Myanmar
items.description: The UN refugee agency, UNHCR, has voiced concern over Malaysia’s decision to return 1,476 people to Myanmar amid an ongoing civil war and a dire human rights and humanitarian situation.
